title: the-cli-and-web-server-reach-devices-without-a-private-ground-loop
intention: Clients reach devices over the bus without building a private GroundLoopDevice, so loop.py and staleness.py can be deleted and the heartbeat is the only ground loop there is.
why: bae622881f03 (PROVED 2026-09-30) made the ground loop a heartbeat and nothing else, but left loop.py standing because bus_client._wire still builds a GroundLoopDevice for every client: connect_bus, connect_system (the web server's listener) and reach. So there are still two ground loops: the resident heartbeat, and a private in-process one inside each client, which on connect_system fires one full beat of every probe on the tree at web-server start. The lived symptom: a mind reading 'ground loop' finds two meanings, and the web server's start pays a whole old-style beat.
traces_to: Law 1 and Law 6 via ticket bae622881f03 (PROVED 2026-09-30): the ground loop is only a heartbeat, one process, and Akien ruled 'the web server launch should be from the web server shim ... same with bus handling ... each device should check for mail ... in the device, not the ground loop'. A second in-process GroundLoopDevice inside every client is a second ground loop.
how: bus_client's three faces (connect_bus, connect_system, reach) stop constructing GroundLoopDevice in _wire: they build a BusDevice, load each named device's shim from disk (_load_device_shim, unchanged) and pulse only those shims to wire delivery, as reach already does. The web server's roster source (server.py:68 calls roster_source.roster()) becomes a small roster object over the device list on disk (cairn.tools.base.deviceness), not a loop. The 'ground_loop' special case in _wire goes, with ground_loop/shim.py. Then delete ground_loop/loop.py and staleness.py, and the proofs that exist only to test them (ground_loop/proofs/test_ground_loop.py's GroundLoopDevice teeth, test_discovery.py's loop half), and re-point the bus/web_server/system_rackmount proofs that construct GroundLoopDevice(bus=bus) at the loop-free wiring.
falsifier: Proof cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_the_wiring_needs_no_loop.py: (1) importing bus_client and calling reach/connect_bus/connect_system never imports cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.loop (sys.modules check in a subprocess); (2) connect_system returns a roster whose device list equals deviceness membership; (3) reach('<a device with shim>') wires delivery so request() answers, not a timeout; (4) loop.py and staleness.py do not exist, and grep for GroundLoopDevice|ground_loop.loop|ground_loop.staleness over cairn/ bin/ skills/ *.py is empty. Live horizon: the web server starts via its shim and its nav renders devices; the heartbeat's liveness.json stays one pid.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED
watchme: none, because the standing watcher is cairn/tools/bus_client/probes/a_client_reaches_and_never_beats.py, re-aimed by this ticket at the loop-free wiring, and the heartbeat's own record ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json shows one pid.
assumption_check: (1) _load_device_shim(name, bus) builds every named shim from bus alone; only 'ground_loop' needed the loop, and that branch goes with ground_loop/shim.py. (2) Pulsing an addressed shim once is what wires its delivery (reach's docstring, measured 2026-09-07). connect_bus/connect_system keep doing that for the devices they name, so mail still flows. (3) The web server's nav needs only a device list; deviceness.py composes discovery.device_folders for membership. (4) discovery.py stays: the heartbeat imports pulse_sites/load_pulse from it.
missing_check: (a) cairn/tools/bus_client/probes/a_client_reaches_and_never_beats.py and its proof monkeypatch GroundLoopDevice.beat to prove a client never beats; they must assert the new invariant instead (the wiring imports no ground_loop.loop). (b) The bus proofs test_delivery/test_first_rider/test_exchange/test_announce_menu construct GroundLoopDevice(bus=bus) only to pulse shims; they re-point to the loop-free wiring. (c) The system_rackmount and web_server proofs build GroundLoopDevice() as a roster; they re-point to the roster object. (d) cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_device_logs_unwired.py lists GroundLoopDevice among classes; drop it there.

decisions.text: The proof is written and committed red at 2a99235e: cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_the_wiring_needs_no_loop.py (FAILURES/ok() pattern: module-level FAILURES; ok(name, passed, detail) prints '  ok   <name>' or '  RED  <name>' and appends on a fail, never raises; main() returns 1 if FAILURES else 0). Clause 1 runs the three faces in a subprocess and demands the old loop module absent from sys.modules; clause 2 demands connect_system(beat=False)'s second value answer roster() with devices == sorted(fitted_device_ids()); clause 3 demands reach('ground_loop') answer verb 'liveness' with a body carrying 'verdict'; clause 4 demands loop.py and staleness.py absent and the grep over cairn/ bin/ skills/ *.py for GroundLoopDevice | ground_loop.loop | ground_loop.staleness empty. The builder must not edit the proof.

New cairn/tools/bus_client/roster.py: class DeviceRoster(bus, root=None) — root defaults to bus_client._CLASS_ROOT. hold(shim) keeps a held shim, idempotent by device_id. shim_for(name) returns the held shim; else the concrete shim from bus_client._load_device_shim(name, bus); else, when name is in cairn.tools.base.deviceness.fitted_device_ids(root), a DiscoveredShim(name, str(folder), bus=bus) (cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.discovered; folder from discovery.device_folders(root), the probes folder's parent as the loop passed it); else None — every answer found is cached as held. roster() returns {'devices': [{'device': d, 'awake': bool(getattr(held.get(d), 'running', False))} for d in sorted(fitted_device_ids(root))]} — the same dict shape server.py already reads (no 'beats' key; server.py reads only 'devices'; verify with grep before relying on it).

bus_client._wire(devices, beat) builds BusDevice() and DeviceRoster(bus), holds BusShim(bus, roster) (BusShim reads only heartbeat.shim_for), then for each named device holds roster.shim_for(name) when not None — no 'ground_loop' special case and no import of the old loop or discovery.discover. It returns (bus, roster). With beat=True it pulses each named shim, then the BusShim, once with datetime.now(timezone.utc) — that is the whole of 'beat' now. reach(*devices) keeps its LookupError for a name with no shim and pulses only the named shims. connect_bus returns bus; connect_system returns (bus, roster); rewrite the three docstrings to say so and drop the beat-cost history paragraphs that describe the loop. web_server/listener.py stays unchanged: 'ground_loop' now resolves through its own shim.py like any other device.

The builder_check line 'DELETE shim.py' is superseded, because the Akien ruling this ticket carries says the heartbeat's web pane is a template that reads the liveness JSON, and clause 3 of the proof reaches ground_loop's own shim. Move liveness_pane_data(now, home=None) verbatim from loop.py into liveness.py. Rewrite ground_loop/shim.py as GroundLoopShim(BaseShim) with __init__(self, bus=None) (the standard loader contract, obj(bus=bus)), device_id 'ground_loop', and _start_device returning a read-only BaseDevice subclass HeartbeatPage whose declared_panes() is the one liveness pane exactly as loop.py declared it (kind 'liveness', label 'Liveness', handler lambda: liveness_pane_data(datetime.now(timezone.utc).astimezone())), declared_verbs() is {'liveness': lambda envelope: liveness_pane_data(datetime.now(timezone.utc).astimezone())}, and intention/state/settings copied from loop.py's, minus any beat or subscription claim. No probes, no bus writes, no beat.

Delete ground_loop/loop.py, staleness.py and proofs/test_staleness.py. In proofs/test_ground_loop.py delete the teeth that construct or beat GroundLoopDevice and test_the_self_subscription_is_inert_under_the_beat; keep the liveness, guard and claim teeth (bae622881f03 clause 7 test_the_doors_loser_reports_from_the_record_and_exits_distinctly stays); re-point the pane teeth to import liveness_pane_data from liveness and write their record with write_liveness(now, {}, pid, home), and the page tooth to GroundLoopShim() with shim.active_page(). In test_discovery.py delete the loop half (_loop and the staleness tooth). Every other proof that built GroundLoopDevice(bus=bus) + subscribe + beat now pulses its shims directly (shim.on_pulse(now)), with BusShim(bus, DeviceRoster(bus)) where it needed delivery. Reword docstrings and probe prose that name the loop; drop 'GroundLoopDevice' from test_heartbeat.py's banned list (the grep would hit it). Reseal every re-pointed proof with python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --seal <proof>.

After the build: restart the web server the usual way and confirm its nav renders a device list (curl the root page); ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json keeps one pid across three beats; the ground_loop page shows the Liveness pane.

Correction to the roster decision: the DiscoveredShim's folder is the registration folder itself — the probes/ folder path exactly as discovery.device_folders(root) yields it (str(folder)), which is what the loop passed as entry['folder'] — not its parent. Every fitted id has such a folder, because fitted_device_ids is built from that same walk.

This supersedes D3's 'stays unchanged' for the listener. In cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py main(), the call becomes '_bus, roster = connect_system(devices=["librarian", "trouble"])' and 'WebServerDevice(roster, harbor_source=harbor_source(), port=args.port)', with a two-line comment above it: no device is special-cased; the roster lists every fitted device and loads a shim from disk the first time its page or its mail asks for one (ticket efb670ff1dd8). 'ground_loop' is dropped from the list because its shim now loads from disk like any other; librarian and trouble stay named so their delivery is wired at start. In server.py, only the docstring lines that call the roster source 'the ground_loop' are reworded to 'a DeviceRoster'; no logic changes.

DeviceRoster.pulse(now, context=None) pulses the HELD shims in the order they were held. _wire holds BusShim(bus, roster) first and then each named device's shim, so with beat=True the BusShim is pulsed first, as the old loop did. This supersedes D3's 'named shims first, then BusShim'. A shim that raises gives {"device": id, "outcome": "refused", "error": "<Type>: <msg>"}, and the others are still pulsed. The return value is {"pulsed": [held ids in order], "pulses": [each shim's on_pulse return]}.
